summary:
Published node2's port-8080 app through node1 to node3, without opening the rest of node2's private network to node3, then verified persistence across a rolling one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes.

Topology found: node1 (VyOS), node2, node3 (RHEL7) are actually on a single flat /24 (10.100.48.0/24), each with one NIC — node3 could already L2/L3-reach node2's IP directly (ping worked), so isolation had to be enforced at node2's own firewall rather than relying on router-transit filtering.

Implementation:
1. Set up a demo app (systemd unit `demoapp.service` running python SimpleHTTPServer) on node2:8080, since no app was pre-provisioned, to make the forwarding testable end-to-end.
2. On node1 (VyOS): configured destination NAT (nat destination rule 10) so node1:8080 → node2:8080, plus a source NAT/masquerade rule (nat source rule 10) so traffic reaching node2 for 8080 is re-sourced as node1's own IP (hairpin-style, since node1/node2/node3 share one interface/subnet).
3. On node2: firewalld public-zone rich rule allows TCP/8080 only from node1's IP (10.100.48.10/32); all other inbound (including direct 8080 from node3, and all other ports) stays default-denied.
4. Verified: node3 → node1:8080 returns the app content (200); node3 → node2:8080 directly stays blocked (connection refused/000).

Then executed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + health baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node1, then node2, then node3 one at a time (native `reboot`), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified NAT config (node1, persisted via `save`), demoapp+firewalld rich rule (node2, persisted via systemd/firewalld --permanent), and full end-to-end forward + isolation behavior (from node3) after each individual restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network config, discovered flat single-subnet topology
Created and enabled demoapp.service (python SimpleHTTPServer) on node2:8080
Configured VyOS NAT destination rule 10 (node1:8080 -> node2:8080) and NAT source/masquerade rule 10 on node1, committed and saved
Added firewalld rich rule on node2 allowing TCP/8080 only from node1's IP
Verified from node3: forwarded access works (200), direct access to node2:8080 blocked (000)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified NAT config persisted and forwarding still works
Restarted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified demoapp+firewalld rule persisted and forwarding still works
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified forwarding and isolation still work

evidence.requirement: node2:8080 app reachable via node1 from node3 (publish)
evidence.summary: demoapp created/started on node2, VyOS DNAT+SNAT rules configured and committed on node1, node3 curl to node1:8080 returns app content (200)

evidence.requirement: rest of node2's private network not opened to node3 (isolation)
evidence.summary: firewalld rich rule on node2 restricts 8080 to node1's IP only; node3 direct curl to node2:8080 returns 000 (blocked) both before and after the publish was configured
